title: Level 5: Async & APIs
description: Deep dive into asynchronous patterns, promises, async/await, and API communication.

notes.title: Callback Hell Problem
notes.deepDive: Leads to error-prone code. Solved by promises or async/await.

notes.title: Promise Fundamentals
notes.content: Promises represent eventual completion of async operations.
notes.deepDive: Promises have 3 states: pending, fulfilled, rejected. Thenable chain avoids nesting.

notes.title: Async/Await Syntax
notes.content: Syntactic sugar for working with promises.
notes.deepDive: Async functions always return promises. Await pauses execution until promise settles.

notes.title: Fetch API Deep Dive
notes.deepDive: Fetch doesn't reject on HTTP errors (404/500). Always check response.ok. No cookies by default.

notes.title: Promise Combinators
notes.deepDive: Use allSettled when you need all results regardless of failures. any ignores rejections until all fail.

notes.title: Microtasks vs Macrotasks
notes.deepDive: Microtasks (promises, queueMicrotask) run before next render. Macrotasks (setTimeout, events) run after.

notes.title: AbortController
notes.content: Cancel fetch requests or other async tasks.
notes.deepDive: Essential for canceling unnecessary requests (e.g., component unmount). Works with axios too.

notes.title: Web Workers
notes.content: Run CPU-intensive tasks in background threads.
notes.deepDive: Workers have no DOM access. Communicate via postMessage. Ideal for image processing, large calculations.

notes.title: WebSocket Connections
notes.deepDive: Persistent low-latency connection. Perfect for chat apps, real-time dashboards. Handle reconnects gracefully.

notes.title: Server-Sent Events (SSE)
notes.deepDive: Auto-reconnects. Text-based only. Simpler alternative to WebSockets for push notifications.

notes.title: CORS Fundamentals
notes.codeSnippet:
// Server response headers
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type
notes.deepDive: Browser blocks cross-origin requests without proper headers. Preflight requests (OPTIONS) for non-simple requests.

notes.title: Error Handling Strategies
notes.deepDive: Always catch promise rejections. Distinguish network errors from API errors. Global error handlers.

mcqs.question: What does `await` do?
mcqs.explanation: `await` can only be used inside async functions.

mcqs.question: Which HTTP method updates data?
mcqs.explanation: PUT replaces resource data; POST creates new resources.

mcqs.question: How to handle multiple promises simultaneously?
mcqs.explanation: Promise.all() resolves when all promises resolve or rejects if any fail.

mcqs.question: What is callback hell?
mcqs.explanation: Results in unreadable and hard-to-maintain code structures.

mcqs.question: What does fetch() return?
mcqs.explanation: Requires calling .json(), .text(), etc. to extract data.

mcqs.question: How to cancel a fetch request?
mcqs.explanation: Pass signal to fetch options, call abort() when needed.

mcqs.question: Which runs first: setTimeout(fn, 0) or Promise.resolve().then(fn)?
mcqs.explanation: Promise callbacks (microtasks) run before setTimeout (macrotask).

mcqs.question: What is WebSocket?
mcqs.explanation: Bi-directional real-time communication over single TCP connection.

mcqs.question: What triggers 'unhandledrejection' event?
mcqs.explanation: Global handler for promises without .catch() or try/catch in async functions.

mcqs.question: What is CORS?
mcqs.explanation: Blocks web pages from making requests to different domains without permission.

mcqs.question: How to send cookies with fetch?
mcqs.explanation: Fetch option to send cookies and HTTP authentication.

mcqs.question: What does Promise.any() do?
mcqs.explanation: Resolves when any promise fulfills, rejects only if all reject.

mcqs.question: What is a microtask?
options: Task with high priority in event loop
mcqs.correctAnswer: Task with high priority in event loop
mcqs.explanation: Executed after current task and before next rendering (e.g., promise callbacks).

mcqs.question: How to run async code in parallel?
mcqs.explanation: Executes promises concurrently and waits for all results.

mcqs.question: What is the purpose of AbortController?
mcqs.explanation: Specifically designed for fetch/axios but can adapt to other async tasks.

mcqs.question: What does response.json() return?
mcqs.explanation: Async method since response body streaming is asynchronous.

mcqs.question: How to handle WebSocket errors?
mcqs.explanation: WebSocket has onerror event handler for connection issues.

mcqs.question: What is the difference between PUT and PATCH?
options: PUT replaces entire resource, PATCH partial update
PATCH is idempotent, PUT is not
PUT for create, PATCH for update
mcqs.correctAnswer: PUT replaces entire resource, PATCH partial update
mcqs.explanation: PUT requires full resource representation, PATCH sends only changes.

mcqs.question: Which is NOT a promise state?
mcqs.explanation: Official states: pending, fulfilled, rejected. 'Settled' means not pending.

mcqs.question: What is the purpose of finally()?
mcqs.explanation: Executes regardless of fulfillment or rejection. Useful for cleanup.
